The direct consumers of `OrderSetService.saveOrderSet` in the REST module are two resource classes in `openmrs-module-webservices.rest`, plus one test. Both resources are the `openmrs1_12` versions of the `/ws/rest/v1` order set resources. I searched the whole webservices.rest repo for `saveOrderSet` and found no other callers.

**Confirmed affected (REST module):**

1. **`OrderSetResource1_12.save`** (`openmrs-module-webservices.rest/omod/src/main/java/org/openmrs/module/webservices/rest/web/v1_0/resource/openmrs1_12/OrderSetResource1_12.java:57-72`). This is the `orderset` resource's create/update path. It resolves member concepts and order types by UUID, then returns `Context.getOrderSetService().saveOrderSet(orderSet)` directly (line 71). Any change to the return value, the persistence or retire semantics, or the exceptions thrown will show up in the `POST`/`PUT` responses for `/ws/rest/v1/orderset`.

2. **`OrderSetMemberResource1_12`** (`.../openmrs1_12/OrderSetMemberResource1_12.java`), which is a sub-resource of the order set. It calls `saveOrderSet` in three places:
   - `delete` (lines 151-155): retires a member, then saves the parent order set.
   - `save` (lines 162-168): adds the member to its parent, then saves the parent.
   - `purge` (lines 170-175): removes the member, then saves the parent.

   Changes to how `saveOrderSet` handles membership or retirement will affect the `/orderset/{uuid}/member` create, update, delete and purge endpoints.

3. **`OrderSetMemberController1_12Test.java:85`** (`openmrs-module-webservices.rest/omod/src/test/java/org/openmrs/module/webservices/rest/web/v1_0/controller/openmrs1_12/OrderSetMemberController1_12Test.java`). This test calls `saveOrderSet` to set up data, so it will fail if the behaviour changes.

**Core declarations the REST module depends on (`openmrs-core`):**

- `api/src/main/java/org/openmrs/api/OrderSetService.java:51` is the interface declaration.
- `api/src/main/java/org/openmrs/api/impl/OrderSetServiceImpl.java:47-50` is the implementation. It delegates to `saveOrderSetInternal`, which is private (line 79). `retireOrderSet` (lines 57-65) and `unretireOrderSet` (lines 72-74) also go through `saveOrderSetInternal`, not `saveOrderSet`. A change to `saveOrderSetInternal` therefore affects the REST module through those two paths too, even though they do not call `saveOrderSet` directly.

**Likely but not verified:**

- The `/ws/rest/v1` HTTP endpoints for order sets are the consumers of the two resources above. I did not check the Spring controllers or the OpenAPI/metadata definitions, so I have not confirmed the exact URL mapping.
- The openmrs-esm-* frontends (for example `openmrs-esm-form-builder`, `openmrs-esm-patient-chart`) may call these endpoints. I did not search them for `orderset` usage, so this is unverified.

**Not checked:**

- `openmrs-module-ordertemplates`, `openmrs-module-metadataexport` and other modules could call `saveOrderSet` through the service. I searched only webservices.rest and the core declarations, not every repository.
- Dynamic lookups such as `Context.getService(OrderSetService.class)` or reflection, and the `OrderSetDAO` javadoc reference, were not analysed beyond the grep results.
